name: Character Strengths Test
tagline: Find out which core virtues make you who you are.
intro: Across cultures and centuries, six core virtues come back again and again: wisdom, courage, humanity, justice, temperance and transcendence. This test shows which of them are most alive in you. Rate 100 short statements about how you think and act. It takes about five minutes and gives you a clear picture of your signature strengths and how to use them more.
seoTitle: Character Strengths Test: Discover your core virtues
seoDescription: Which virtues define you? Take this free 5-minute character strengths test on wisdom, courage, humanity, justice, temperance and transcendence.

wisdom.name: Wisdom
wisdom.short: Curiosity, creativity, good judgement, love of learning and perspective.
wisdom.low: Wisdom is not one of the virtues you lean on most right now. You may prefer action and practical results over reflecting, studying or exploring ideas. That keeps you grounded, but you might miss useful insights. Try one small habit: before a decision that matters, list the arguments for and against on paper. You could also pick one topic you are curious about and spend fifteen minutes a week learning about it.
wisdom.mid: Wisdom is a solid part of your character. You can be curious and thoughtful, and you often think things through before acting, though not in every situation. This makes you a sensible sounding board for others. To grow this virtue, deliberately seek out views that differ from your own, for example by reading a well-argued opinion you disagree with. Ask yourself regularly what you have learned this week and how it changes your view.
wisdom.high: Wisdom is one of your signature virtues. You are curious, open to evidence and able to see the bigger picture, and people value your advice and fresh ideas. Use this strength deliberately: offer to mentor someone, take on problems that need creative thinking, or share what you learn in a blog, talk or conversation. Watch that your love of thinking does not delay action or make you seem distant; sometimes a good-enough answer now beats a perfect one later.

courage.name: Courage
courage.short: Bravery, perseverance, honesty and zest for life.
courage.low: Courage is currently a quieter virtue in your profile. You may avoid conflict, struggle to keep going when things get hard or feel your energy is low. This is often situational rather than a fixed trait. Start small: choose one minor fear or difficult conversation and face it this week. Break bigger goals into very small steps so finishing feels achievable, and notice how each small act of bravery builds confidence for the next one.
courage.mid: Courage is a solid part of your character. You can speak up, persist and be honest when it really matters, even if it does not always come easily. Build on this by noticing the situations where you hold back and asking what you would do if you were not afraid. Take care of your energy as well, through sleep, movement and things you look forward to, because zest makes bravery and perseverance much easier.
courage.high: Courage is one of your signature virtues. You speak up for what is right, keep going through setbacks, tell the truth and approach life with energy. People see you as genuine and dependable. Put this strength to work on causes and goals that truly matter to you, and use it to support others who find it harder to speak up. Make sure your honesty comes with tact, and allow yourself to rest so your drive does not turn into exhaustion.

humanity.name: Humanity
humanity.short: Love, kindness and understanding of other people.
humanity.low: Humanity is a quieter virtue in your profile at the moment. You may value independence, keep people at a certain distance or focus more on tasks than on feelings. That can make you efficient and self-reliant. Still, close bonds are one of the strongest sources of wellbeing. Try one small act of kindness each day, or ask a friend a deeper question and really listen. Small steps can make connection feel more natural.
humanity.mid: Humanity is a solid part of your character. You care about people, can be kind and generous and usually pick up on what others feel, while also keeping healthy boundaries. To develop this virtue further, make a habit of telling people what you appreciate about them. Notice moments when you are too busy to really listen, and practise giving your full attention for a few minutes, without phones or distractions.
humanity.high: Humanity is one of your signature virtues. You love deeply, act with kindness and understand people well, which makes others feel seen and cared for. Use this strength in roles and relationships where empathy matters, such as supporting colleagues, volunteering or mediating conflicts. Be mindful that caring for everyone can drain you. Set limits on what you give, and let the people close to you care for you too.

justice.name: Justice
justice.short: Fairness, teamwork and leadership that serves the group.
justice.low: Justice is a quieter virtue in your profile right now. You may prefer working alone, focus on your own goals or feel less drawn to leading or organising groups. That independence can be valuable. Still, fairness and teamwork help you build trust and achieve more together. Try volunteering for a shared task, and when you make decisions involving others, ask yourself whether everyone affected would see the outcome as fair.
justice.mid: Justice is a solid part of your character. You value fairness, can work well in a team and step up to lead when needed. This makes you a reliable team member. To grow this virtue, take responsibility for including others: invite quieter people into discussions and give credit generously. You can also practise leading in low-pressure situations, such as organising a group activity, to build confidence in bringing people together.
justice.high: Justice is one of your signature virtues. You treat people fairly, are a loyal team player and know how to bring a group together around a goal. Others trust you to be impartial. Use this strength in roles where fairness and cooperation matter, such as coordinating projects, chairing meetings or standing up for equal treatment. Be careful not to take on every injustice alone, and remember that fairness also includes being fair to yourself.

temperance.name: Temperance
temperance.low: Temperance is a quieter virtue in your profile at the moment. You may act on impulse, find it hard to let go of hurt or enjoy being recognised for what you do. Spontaneity has its charms, but it can also lead to regret. Try a simple pause: count to ten before reacting in a heated moment or making a purchase. Writing down what still bothers you about an old conflict can also help you start letting it go.
temperance.mid: Temperance is a solid part of your character. You can usually control your impulses, stay modest and give people a second chance, though stress can test this. To strengthen this virtue, identify your main triggers, such as tiredness, hunger or certain people, and plan how you will respond in advance. Building one small healthy habit at a time, rather than many at once, is the most reliable way to grow self-discipline.
temperance.high: Temperance is one of your signature virtues. You are forgiving, modest, careful and in control of your impulses, which makes you calm and steady under pressure. People trust you not to overreact. Use this strength in situations that need a cool head, such as negotiations, long-term planning or helping others settle conflicts. Just make sure modesty does not hide your achievements and caution does not stop you from taking worthwhile chances.

transcendence.name: Transcendence
transcendence.short: Gratitude, hope, humour, appreciation of beauty and a sense of meaning.
transcendence.low: Transcendence is a quieter virtue in your profile right now. Life may feel mostly practical, or you may tend to expect the worst and rarely pause to enjoy what is good. That realism has value, but it can make life feel heavy. Try writing down three good things each evening, however small. Spending time in nature or doing something purely for fun can also gently reconnect you with joy and meaning.
transcendence.mid: Transcendence is a solid part of your character. You can feel gratitude, hope and wonder, and you enjoy a good laugh, though daily stress sometimes pushes these feelings aside. To grow this virtue, build small rituals into your week: a walk without your phone, a thank-you message to someone or a moment to reflect on what gives your life meaning. These habits strengthen resilience in harder times.
transcendence.high: Transcendence is one of your signature virtues. You notice beauty, feel grateful, stay hopeful and bring humour and a sense of meaning to life. This makes you resilient and uplifting to be around. Use it to support others during difficult times, for example by helping them see a way forward or sharing a moment of lightness. Be careful not to brush aside real problems; hope works best when it is paired with honest action.

summary: Everyone has all six virtues to some degree; what differs is which ones you rely on most. Below you see how strongly each virtue shows up in your answers, with your strongest one highlighted as your signature virtue. Lower scores are not weaknesses, but areas you can grow when you choose to.
